dedupe_keys.name: noaa soil freeze thaw heat model

description: SoilFreezeThaw is a one-dimensional soil heat-transport model from NOAA's Office of Water Prediction. It solves a vertical diffusion equation with implicit interior steps and semi-implicit surface and bottom boundaries. Users provide soil properties, moisture profiles and weather or boundary forcing; outputs are changing soil-temperature and freeze-thaw conditions by depth and time. Geographic coverage is a selected site or grid column. Apache-2.0 source, an INSTALL guide and standalone and framework examples are public. The README describes coupling to the NextGen water framework as well as synthetic and real forcing tests. A limitation is that a single column omits lateral heat and water movement, so roadbed or pipeline applications need site-specific checks. The model can support freeze-related stress analysis for water lines, roads and foundations. The related catalogue Alaska permafrost record is a separate exposure dataset, not a SoilFreezeThaw run. No forcing, compiler binary or output was downloaded.
inputs: Soil properties, moisture and thermal boundary forcing
